Definition of Summary


• A summary is a brief restatement of the
 essential thought of a longer composition. It
 reproduces the theme of the original with as
 few words as possible. When one writes a
 summary, one should not interpret or
 comment. All one has to do is to give the gist
 (general meaning) of the author’s exact and
 essential meaning.

Uses of Summary Writing


• Summary writing is a very good exercise for
 improving reading comprehension.
• Summary writing is also helpful to
 composition writing.
• Summary writing is necessary for your future
 professions.

Features Of Summary
Brief

Complete

1. Reading
• First read the passage through carefully to get
 the gist of it.
• Give a title to your summary.
• You should now be in a position to decide what
 parts of the passage are essential and what
 parts are comparatively unimportant and can
 be omitted without much loss.
• Write down in brief notes the main points: the
 subject, the title, and the essential or important
 details.

2. Writing

• A summary should usually be about one-third to
 one-fourth as long as the original passage, but
 for a summary of a novel or a play, one-
 hundredth or even one-thousandth of the
 length of the original book.
• The summary should be all in your own words.
• You should follow the logical order of the original
 passage, if possible.

3. Revision

• Continue to compress it by omitting
 unnecessary words and phrases.
• Correct mistakes in spelling and grammar.

Examples of compression

• His courage in battle might without exaggeration be
 called lion-like.
He was very brave in battle.
• John fell into the river and, before help could reach
 him, he sank.
John was drowned in the river.
• She brought home several Chinese and English
 novels, a few copies of Time and Newsweek, and
 some textbooks. She intended to read all of them
 during the winter vacation.
She brought home a lot of books and magazines to
read during the vacation.
